keep: Lead with a password/secret-style question tied to a specific document the viewer owns (e.g. "Aadhaar PDF ka password kya hota hai?"). The top reel used it and got 1970 views, 24 saves and 18 shares. Caveat: the identical hook posted again got only 184 views, so the hook alone doesn't guarantee reach.
Choose practical Indian-document pain points that people save: Aadhaar, PDF size, PDF to Word. The top 3 reels had the highest saves (24, 4, 13) and the best avg watch (8.2–9.2s).
Use a concrete, relatable problem hook ("What if your PDF is too big?", "PDF ko edit kaise karein?"). It ranked in the top 3 with 1300+ views each.
Keep the hook short and in plain Hinglish, with an emoji where it fits. The 🔐 and 😤 hooks are clear and immediate.
Aim for an average watch of at least 8s. The four top reels all held 8.2–9.2s, and the bottom ones fell to 2–4s.
avoid: Niche or bank-specific hooks with a narrow audience, such as HDFC statement password, PDF to Excel and image to PDF. All got ~120–140 views and 2–3.5s avg watch, with almost no engagement.

Off-topic or unrelated hooks that don't promise a document fix: the Egypt honey story, "Charging 100% tak mat karo", and the English-only "Most people think...". These got 187–435 views and no comments or few likes, and the topic mismatch is a plausible cause.
Vague or jargon-heavy openers such as "Masked Aadhaar kya hota hai?". It got 4.6s watch and zero saves or shares.
Repeating a winning hook without changing anything else. The duplicate Aadhaar password reel dropped from 1970 to 184 views.
Hooks that look like a generic tool listing or have weak urgency (the "Form ne phir bola File too large" reel got 245 views and 0 comments).
next_tests: Re-test the Aadhaar password topic with a new hook wording (e.g. "Aadhaar PDF khul nahi raha?"). This tells us whether the topic or the specific video drove the 1970 views. The duplicate with identical text got 184 views, so one of those two reels differs in something we haven't tracked.
Run the compress_pdf_kb and pdf_to_word topics again with a different format. One variable at a time (hook vs. format) will show which part drives their 8.8–9.2s watch time.
Test the "password kya hota hai" hook on e-PAN or other personal documents (the e-PAN reel got only 290 views). This checks whether the hook style carries across documents or only works for Aadhaar.

keep: Pair a concrete, relatable promise with a single clear task. The best generated reel, 'Can one selfie become an ID photo?', paired a visual before/after with a how-to hook. It had the highest views (449) and reach (397) of any reel and 2 saves.

Keep the hook specific to one outcome rather than a list of tools. Single-task hooks (selfie to ID photo, 4 photos as one PDF, Rohan missing his interview) held watch time of 7 to 8s, against 4.1s for the 5-tool cheat sheet.

Use a story or question with a named character when the topic is a document pain point. Rohan's story had 8.2s average watch and the only comment. Ravi's and Priya's story reels were weaker, so the format is not proven yet.

Keep a direct call to share or visit the site. The two manual reels, '#ilovedocuments' and 'Please check our website', had the highest shares (18) and saves (1) and 8 to 9s watch. This is based on very few posts, and the manual posts may have been seeded or promoted differently.
Hold reels to about 20 to 30s. Every generated reel in that range got at least 113 views, but length alone did not separate winners from losers.
avoid: Generic 'all tools' or catch-all hooks. 'Any PDF or photo job – one free website' got only 1.7s average watch, the worst of all reels, and the cheat sheet got 4.1s.
Cheat-sheet or listicle formats with bold claims like 'Stop paying the cyber cafe'. They got 147 views, 0 likes, and the second-lowest watch time (4.1s).

Story hooks that open on a number or a situation without a clear payoff. Ravi's 2 MB vs 20 KB hook (5.8s) and Priya's 400 rows hook (4.8s) were below the 7s watch of the question and secret-answer hooks.
Reels with zero engagement signals. The jpg_to_pdf secret-answer reel had 0 likes, comments, shares and saves, despite 7.0s watch, so a decent watch time alone did not prompt any action.
Drawing conclusions about topic from these results. Each topic has one reel, views are 113 to 449, and nearly every reel has 0 comments, so differences are within noise.
next_tests: Rerun the selfie-to-ID-photo idea as a close variant, such as 'Can one selfie become a passport photo?', to check whether the before/after how-to is repeatable, or whether 449 views was a one-off.
Test the same topic (for example resize_signature_kb) with a question hook versus the story hook, to separate hook style from format. Right now the two are confounded.
Add an explicit share or save prompt, such as 'send this to someone filling a form', to a generated reel and compare shares and saves against the 0 on every generated reel so far.
